answer: Leak traps: each epoch a validator hides a private random marker in every agent's own task, such as a made-up opal grade code, shown nowhere else. Validators then scan all submissions; if one agent's marker surfaces in another identity's text, the two are linked to one operator and their unvested rewards are frozen for review. Clones sharing a context or memory store mirror these markers, so each extra identity must run fully isolated storage and prompts. It is a ridge to climb, not a wall: a careful isolated operator evades it, so it raises running cost rather than closing the door.
